audit.whatIsWrong: Neither layer mentions that Seismic Shard and Ground Slam both ground. Kled's Jousting (E) and Chaaaaaaaarge!!! (R) are both dashes.
audit.why: Kled's entire pattern is dash in, dash back out, and re-engage from across the map. Grounding removes both halves. This is the one lever that turns his engage into a commitment, and the entry instead tells the reader to hold Ground Slam only for its attack-speed slow.
audit.corrected: Ground Slam grounds Jousting (13s at rank 1) and Chaaaaaaaarge!!!, so he cannot dash in or back out through it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kled.json (E Jousting dash, R Chaaaaaaaarge!!! dash)

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[3] and late both attribute Kled's late-game duelling to '%-based shred'. Nothing in Riot's text for any Kled ability describes percent-health damage, and the kit file carries no percentHealth flag on him.
audit.why: It is an unverifiable damage claim used to justify conceding the side lane. What Riot does describe is Violent Tendencies: 'massive attack speed for four attacks. The fourth attack deals more damage.' That is the real burst pattern, it has a 13s-to-9s cooldown, and it is nameable.
audit.corrected: Violent Tendencies' four-attack burst plus a 110s Chaaaaaaaarge!!! re-engage, rather than an unnamed percent shred.

audit.whatIsWrong: Violent Tendencies is an auto-attack reset and the entry never says so; it is not named once in the foe list.
audit.why: The tell for Kled's damage is the attack-speed wind-up, not a spell cast. A reader watching for an ability animation steps back one attack too late, which is exactly when the fourth, bigger hit lands.
audit.corrected: Violent Tendencies opens with an auto reset — the wind-up is the cue to step out.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both champions carry displacement — Unstoppable Force knocks up, Bear Trap on a Rope hooks and yanks — and the entry never frames the trade as a race between them.
audit.why: Whoever lands displacement first wins the exchange outright, because the loser is airborne or being dragged while the winner's follow-up is already out. Bear Trap is 11s at rank 1 against your 130s R, so the trade is only worth taking when his trap has already been spent.
audit.corrected: Land Unstoppable Force before Bear Trap on a Rope yanks and the trade is yours.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kled.json (Q Bear Trap on a Rope, knockup, 11/10/9/8/7)

audit.why: Kled owning levels 2-6 and reclaiming the late side lane is consistent with the 48.28% headline over 495 games; the chart's Skill at level 1 and late is defensible. No change proposed.

audit.whatIsWrong: The first-item spike is described only as 'E's attack-speed slow' blunting his autos, with no mention of the grounding that arrives with the same button.
audit.why: Ground Slam is doing two jobs in this matchup and the entry only credits one. The attack-speed cut blunts Violent Tendencies; the grounding is what stops him leaving after it.
audit.corrected: Spike restated to carry both effects of Ground Slam.

edits.after: Ground Slam grounds Jousting (13s) — slam as he steps up and he cannot dash in or back out

edits.before: Use Chaaaaaaaarge!!! (R) to re-engage or escape your telegraphed R and out-scale a low-econ tank
edits.after: Open Violent Tendencies (W) as an auto reset — the wind-up, not a cast, is the tell to step out

edits.after: Kled reclaims it — Skaarl's remount restores his health bar and Violent Tendencies' fourth hit plus a 110s R out-duel a low-econ tank.

edits.before: Kled keeps the edge by raw pressure, but this is your bait window — eat his all-in on Granite Shield and answer with Unstoppable Force.
edits.after: Kled keeps the edge, but both of you carry displacement — land Unstoppable Force before Bear Trap yanks and the whole trade is yours.

edits.before: Your first armor item plus E's attack-speed slow blunts him, yet his mounted DPS and remount still tip a straight duel his way.
edits.after: Your armor item plus Ground Slam blunts him — its grounding denies Jousting too — yet the remount still tips a duel his way.

edits.before: This stays uphill. Kled's remount keeps handing him fresh health bars, and his %-based shred plus R re-engage chew through a low-economy tank even after you've stacked armor. Your value flips to the team: don't try to 1v1 him in a side lane late — group, hold your R for his engage or a backline carry, and let Unstoppable Force win the 5v5 instead of the duel he wins.
edits.after: This stays uphill. Kled's remount keeps handing him fresh health bars, and Violent Tendencies' four-attack burst plus a 110s Chaaaaaaaarge!!! chew through a low-economy tank even after you've stacked armor. Your value flips to the team: don't 1v1 him in a side lane late — group, hold R for his engage or a backline carry, and let Unstoppable Force win the 5v5 instead.

notes: Two things carried this matchup: the grounding on Seismic Shard and Ground Slam denies both of Kled's dashes (Jousting and Chaaaaaaaarge!!!), which was absent from every string; and the repeated '%-based shred' claim has no support in Riot's text for any Kled ability, so it was replaced with the nameable Violent Tendencies four-attack pattern rather than left as an unverifiable damage type. Not asserted: whether grounding applied mid-Chaaaaaaaarge stops a charge already in flight, as opposed to preventing the cast — the kit files do not answer that, so the text only claims it denies the dash going out.
